newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil still studying coffee for soluble industry.
newsitem.headline: Brazil still studying coffee for soluble industry.

text.p: Brazil's Finance Ministry is still studying a proposal to lend coffee stocks to the soluble industry, a Finance Ministry official said.
The official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said it was possible the ministry might hold meetings next week with officials from the Ministry of Industry and Commerce to discuss the plan.

"There's no fight going on between us. It's possible (there may be meetings next week)," he said, adding that it was not the Finance Ministry which was holding up approval of the proposal but the Ministry of Industry and Commerce.

Earlier, Roberto Abreu, interim head of the National Coffee Department, said through a spokeswoman there was no guarantee officials from the two industries would meet next week over demands by the soluble industry for coffee stocks.
The soluble industry has been threatening to import coffee to meet production demands but has agreed to put that project on hold while Brazil's CDPC coffee council ponders alternative solutions.
A CDPC meeting called for Thursday was apparently cancelled and industry sources said the stock lending plan had been put on hold while the two ministries battled over it.

The CDPC, which groups the private and public sector and is supposed to define national coffee policy, is due to hold its next formal meeting in Santos but no date has been set for it while the soluble industry's problems remain unresolved.
